Food Products Standards & Food Additives Compendium — current chapter index

sections.name: Food Additives
rules: Use of an additive must be technologically justified and must not present an appreciable health risk or mislead the consumer.
Under GMP, use the lowest level necessary to achieve the technological effect.
Food additives shall be of appropriate food-grade quality and comply with applicable identity/purity specifications.
Unless otherwise specified, maximum-use levels in tables are set on the final product as consumed.

Carry-over is permitted only when the additive is permitted in the raw material/ingredient, the ingredient itself does not exceed its applicable maximum, and the level carried into the final food is no greater than expected under proper technological conditions/GMP.
Carry-over is not acceptable for the listed infant/young-child food categories unless an additive provision is expressly specified.

sections.name: Standards of Additives
sections.engine_rule: Chapter 3.2 identity/purity standards qualify the additive itself. Permission to use that additive in a finished food still comes from the applicable product standard and/or Appendix A.

sections.name: Other substances for use in food products
sections.engine_rule: Apply only to the named substances, foods and conditions explicitly specified in Chapter 3.3.

sections.name: Processing Aids
sections.engine_rule: Processing aids are only permitted where expressly allowed. Product/process permissions and residual levels are resolved through the applicable processing-aid provisions and Appendix C.

sequence: Resolve finished-food standardized identity and FCS
Check the vertical product standard for explicit additive permissions, prohibitions or stricter limits
Resolve Appendix A parent-category and sub-category permissions using the hierarchy
Apply the most specific applicable category entry where the same additive appears at multiple hierarchy levels
Apply GMP Table only when the selected FCS is not listed in the Annex to GMP
Check carry-over separately from direct addition
Apply additive identity/purity requirements from Chapter 3.2
Apply applicable labelling declarations and other current FSSAI regulations
precedence: Explicit product-standard prohibition or narrower limit
Most specific Appendix A sub-category permission/limit
GMP Table permission where Annex to GMP does not exclude the FCS
Carry-over only when all Chapter 3.1 carry-over conditions are satisfied
hard_fail_conditions: Additive is not permitted by any applicable direct-addition route
Entered level exceeds the strictest applicable maximum
GMP Table is relied upon for an FCS listed in the Annex to GMP
An additive is used to disguise faulty raw material or undesirable/unhygienic practices

sweetener_classification.caloric_definition: Greater than 2 percent of the caloric value of sucrose per equivalent unit of sweetening capacity.

other_substances.name: Phyto or Plant Stanol

daily_max.basis: calculated as free Phyto or Plant Stanols

portion_rules: A single portion may contain maximum 3 g.
Alternatively, three portions may each contain 1 g.
Where products are not sold in those single-portion formats, clearly indicate the standard portion in g or ml and the amount of free Phyto or Plant Stanols in that portion.
other_substances.label_reference_status: The Chapter 3 source retains a historical Packaging and Labelling cross-reference; current artwork must be validated against the operative Labelling and Display regulations.
other_substances.runtime_status: Exact product-category and serving-size route required before PASS.

other_substances.name: Phyto or Plant Sterol

daily_max.basis: calculated as free Phyto or Plant Sterols

portion_rules: A single portion may contain maximum 3 g.
Alternatively, portions may contain maximum 1 g, with composition and labelling enabling the consumer to restrict intake to maximum 3 g/day.
Where the product is not sold in those portion formats, clearly indicate the standard portion in g or ml and the amount of free Phyto or Plant Sterol in that portion.
additional_conditions: The product must not exceed the applicable Acceptable Daily Intake for Phytosterols.
Current label declarations must be validated under the operative labelling regulation before final approval.
other_substances.label_reference_status: The Chapter 3 source retains a historical Packaging and Labelling cross-reference; current artwork must be validated against the operative Labelling and Display regulations.
other_substances.runtime_status: Exact product-category, non-GM source, ADI and serving-size gates required before PASS.

runtime_policy.other_substances_3_3: Chapter 3.3 named substances never auto-apply solely from ingredient name. PMSV must match the selected product to the exact permission route and evaluate limits, exclusions, source/serving conditions and current labelling before PASS.

identity_purity_standards.name: Sorbitol

identity.appearance: White hygroscopic powder having a sweet taste

requirements.condition: Depending on the method of test used for analysis.

identity_purity_standards.engine_note: This is the identity/purity standard for Sorbitol. Permission to use Sorbitol in a finished food remains governed separately by the applicable product standard and/or Appendix A.

identity_purity_standards.name: Food Colour - Preparation and Mixtures

identity.scope: Preparation containing one or more permitted food colours conforming to the prescribed standard, with permitted diluents/filler materials or both, intended to impart colour to food.
identity.solid_condition: Free from lumps and visible extraneous or foreign matter.

permitted_diluents_fillers: Sodium carbonate and sodium hydrogen carbonate
Glycerol mono, di and tri acetate
identity_purity_standards.additives_condition: May contain permitted additives as applicable under Appendix A and Appendix C.

general_requirements.requirement: Declare total dye content, percent by mass (m/v), on the container label.
For both solid and liquid preparations, the amended clause states the declared value on 'as is' basis.
Must comply with the Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011, as amended.

runtime_policy.permission_to_use_finished_food: Separate Appendix A / product-standard permission is still required.
